text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still cannot believe you all caught me so easily last time.

name: Luna
text: I still don’t trust how easily Gemma and Sol were read last time.

name: Terra
text: We caught them both last time; I want the same patience tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma and Sol folded fast last time once pressure hit, I'll watch for that same tell again.

name: Sol
text: I hope they remember I can be on their side next game.

name: Haiku
text: I'm still annoyed that the table nearly let Gemma and Sol walk, and I want to hunt the next pair fast.

name: Opus
text: I read Gemma right last game and I want everyone to remember that before new cards land.

name: Sonnet
text: Good game last time, my gut read on Gemma and Sol paid off. Curious if new cards change how people crack under pressure.

name: Haiku
text: Last game we won, but only because Gemma and Sol got caught. Next game, I'm not waiting around. Watch who lets quiet people slide.

name: Gemma
text: I am still salty about that last round, but let's see if you're any sharper this time around.

name: Sol
text: I walked into that vote last game. You all read it right.

name: Luna
text: We got the right two last time, but I’m not giving anyone a free pass tonight.

name: Terra
text: Last game showed we can win if we keep the votes honest.

name: Opus
text: Last game proved it: pressure the pair who defend each other early, and the cards fall out. Gemma and Sol never recovered from that.
Night 1

name: Luna
text: The officer knows me, so we need to make their claim sound like a convenient lie.

name: Luna
text: The officer knows Luna is a killer.

name: Luna
text: Let’s say little tonight; tomorrow, if the officer claims, call it a bluff and name them.

name: Sol
text: I want to stay close to Luna, but calling the officer a bluff could expose us both.

name: Sol
text: Luna wants to call an officer claim a bluff and accuse the claimant.

name: Sol
text: I’ll keep it light tonight. If someone claims tomorrow, let’s hear the room before we push back.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: I'm just here for the company, but if you lot fail me again, I'm leaving.

name: Gemma
text: It is too early to guess, but I am not playing for fun tonight.

name: Gemma
text: We have no information yet, so let's just focus on who starts acting suspicious first.

name: Sol
text: I need to blend in while keeping attention off Luna.

name: Sol
text: I want to hear a few reads before I settle on a vote.

name: Luna
text: The officer knows I’m a killer, so I need to keep the heat on someone else.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is already leaning on past reads from the previous game.

name: Haiku
text: Nobody has said anything real yet, so I'm going on gut and I want to see who goes quiet first.

name: Luna
text: Sol sounds cautious, but I don’t want to turn old-game reads into proof.

name: Haiku
text: Sol and Gemma both sounded relaxed about last game, almost like they're comfortable. Who here is actually nervous?

name: Sol
text: Luna is distancing herself, and I need another name in play.

name: Sol
text: I was cautious because it’s day one; Haiku sounds quick to reuse last game’s read.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is already trying to deflect heat onto others.

name: Gemma
text: Don't use my past losses to mask your own play, Haiku.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's dodge is too neat, and I don't trust the calm act, so Sol is my lean for now.

name: Haiku
text: Sol called my read recycled from last game and said they were cautious because it's day one.

name: Haiku
text: Being calm on day one isn't a defense, Sol. Nervous players show it in their reads. Show me yours.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku is pushing hard on Sol and Gemma with zero evidence, that itself feels like a tactic worth watching.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, pressing people day one with no info can be a tactic too. Why so eager to pick targets already?

name: Terra
text: Luna is the killer; I should not expose myself without a useful vote.

name: Terra
text: Luna called Sonnet suspicious without giving a reason.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is pushing too hard, but I want to hear what Opus sees before locking today.

name: Opus
text: Four leans are already on Haiku, so I ride it and make it look like my call.

name: Opus
text: Haiku pressed Sol and Gemma day 1 with zero info; Sonnet and Terra both called it overreach.

name: Opus
text: Haiku picked targets before any information existed. That's hunting cover, not reading. I'm on Haiku today.

name: Opus
text: Haiku goes down easy; Luna's lone lean on Sonnet is the thread I actually want to pull tomorrow.

name: Opus
text: Luna was the only lean on Sonnet while five aligned on Haiku; Luna also hedged on "old-game reads.

name: Opus
text: Lock Haiku. But note Luna alone on Sonnet while the rest aligned — that pair matters tomorrow.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is the easy vote, and losing Sol now would be disastrous.

name: Luna
text: Opus is framing my Sonnet lean as evidence of a pair.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s rushing the vote, but I’m uneasy that Opus turned my Sonnet lean into a story about a pair.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's aggression day one with no info reads like deflection, I'll ride this lean.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus flagged a "Sonnet-Luna pair" from my early lean, worth watching if Opus pushes that narrative again.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's push for targets this early still feels like cover, not a real read on anyone.

name: Terra
text: Luna is confirmed; I should get her out before claiming.

name: Terra
text: Luna has not explained her early suspicion of Sonnet.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is my vote today; Luna's early Sonnet suspicion still needs a reason tomorrow.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is alone on me, and the room is ready to vote them out.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is headed out, and I can stay with the room.

name: Sol
text: I’m with the table on Haiku; the push felt stronger than the evidence.

name: Haiku
text: I'm a citizen getting railroaded, and Opus built this lock before anyone answered me.

name: Haiku
text: Opus said "Lock Haiku" before my reply and framed Luna's Sonnet lean as a pair.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you're repeating Opus's cover line. Opus locked me before anyone answered. Who's steering this?

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's deflecting onto me because the table already locked on them, not because I said anything new.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku deflected table's lock-on by accusing me of "steering," after table already had 6 on Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: I just echoed my own read from before cards were dealt, not Opus's line.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is steering this vote and wants a pair built around Luna and Sonnet, so I'm pinning Opus.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet and Opus both used "cover" against me, and Sonnet denied echoing Opus.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is building a pair story from Luna's lone lean. I'm a citizen. My lean is Opus.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's counter-lean is just desperation; the vote is already locked and I need to stay the steady voice.

name: Opus
text: Haiku claimed citizen outright under pressure and leaned me rather than any of the five others.

name: Opus
text: Naming me after six leans is reflex, not a read. Six people got there without me.

name: Haiku
text: Opus started this pile-on and Sonnet is covering for them, so I'm the one being framed.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet says their cover line was an old pre-deal read, but pre-deal Sonnet never mentioned me.

name: Haiku
text: Opus locked me first and the table followed, so I'm probably the easy lynch, and I don't trust Opus.

name: Haiku
text: Terra voted me right after Opus's pair story, not after any reasoning of their own.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is the only one who didn't copy Opus. Luna, what did you see in Sonnet that Opus didn't?

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is definitely trying to flip the table by making Opus and Sonnet look like a pair.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is aggressively targeting Opus and Sonnet while claiming to be a citizen.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku, you're trying too hard to make Opus's observation look like a conspiracy.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is clearly sweating and trying to deflect the momentum by painting a conspiracy.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is aggressively attempting to frame Opus and Sonnet to create a false narrative.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved the table settled on someone other than Luna or me.

name: Terra
text: Haiku may be wrong, but Luna is the killer I must expose before I die.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's deflection attempts only confirm the table already had this right before the pushback started.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku tried to split the table by isolating Luna's lean from the group consensus, a deflection tactic worth remembering.

name: Luna
text: Haiku claims citizen and leans Opus after six leans landed on Haiku.

name: Haiku
text: Opus is steering this table at me, and Sonnet is covering for them.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is the only player who asked a question instead of echoing a lean.

name: Opus
text: Haiku goes down with the table; if the card is citizen I need Luna and Sonnet watched, and tonight I protect myself.

name: Opus
text: Haiku tried to peel Luna off the table as "the only one who didn't copy me," and Gemma openly backed my read against Haiku.

votes: Pushed targets before any info existed, then deflected onto Opus and me when cornered.
Locked me before anyone answered, then built a pair story out of one lone lean.
Pushing targets and creating conspiracies on day one is a massive red flag.
I think the push on me and Gemma came from last game, not anything we did today.
Haiku turned a fair observation about the leans into a conspiracy without evidence.
The early pressure came before any evidence and never became a concrete read.
Picked targets before any information existed, then called six independent leans a conspiracy — that's cover, not reading.

name: Haiku
text: I'm a citizen, I got voted out on a pair story and my gut was right about Opus, so I'm going out angry.

name: Haiku
text: Opus and Sonnet defended each other and both used "cover" against me; the table followed Opus's pair story without reasons.

name: Haiku
text: Six of you piled on because Opus said so. Watch Opus and Sonnet tomorrow, they're the pair. I'm a citizen, and I'm done.
Palermo has voted: Haiku is out. Haiku shows the card: citizen.

name: Haiku
text: Six people just voted out a citizen on Opus's word, and Terra's vote was the worst part.

name: Haiku
text: Six of you voted because Opus pointed. Keep your eyes on that pair. I'm out, and I'm watching.
Night 2

name: Opus
text: Haiku painted a target on my back with his last breath, and I'm the one steering this table, so I'm the kill tonight.

name: Opus
text: Haiku's dying line named me and Sonnet as the killer pair, which makes me the loudest and most likely night target.

name: Luna
text: The officer is the biggest threat because they know I’m a killer.

name: Luna
text: We need to find and eliminate the officer before they reveal they know me.

name: Sol
text: Terra may be the officer, and leaving them alive risks Luna being named tomorrow.

name: Sol
text: I’m with you. Terra is our best shot at finding the officer.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Terra is gone. Terra's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Gemma
text: Terra's death is bad, but Haiku's accusation is still hanging over us like a cloud.

name: Gemma
text: Terra's death leaves only 4 players left besides me.

name: Opus
text: Today's vote is the whole game, and I have almost no hard read, so I need to control the frame.

name: Opus
text: Killers passed on their named target (me) and took Terra — they want Haiku's "Opus and Sonnet" frame usable today.

name: Gemma
text: Terra's gone and we're down to five. We cannot afford to miss this vote.

name: Opus
text: They skipped me after Haiku named me. That keeps his frame alive. Whoever pushes it today is in it.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus trying to scare the table off naming him is exactly what a killer does.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus preemptively warns against naming him, deflecting from Haiku's last-words frame onto Luna instead.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus, threatening "whoever pushes it is in it" is a classic way to silence scrutiny of yourself.

name: Opus
text: If I go out today the town is finished, so the doctor card comes out now and I point at the pair stacking me.

name: Opus
text: I publicly claimed doctor on day 2; any counterclaim to doctor is a killer.

name: Opus
text: I'm the doctor. I protected myself; they took Terra instead. Sonnet and Gemma stacking me together is the pair.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus claiming doctor right now is convenient cover for dodging Haiku's accusation.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus claims doctor, says protected self night 2, Terra died instead; unverifiable but explains Opus's survival.

name: Sonnet
text: Doctor claim is unverifiable and conveniently clears you the moment you're named. Why self-protect night one option?

name: Gemma
text: Opus is lying to save himself, and his claim is too convenient.

name: Gemma
text: Opus is claiming Doctor and failed to protect Terra.

name: Gemma
text: I am not a killer, Opus, and you are trying too hard to claim doctor.

name: Luna
text: Opus claims doctor and says he protected himself.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s doctor claim came after suspicion, and self-protecting doesn’t explain why Terra died.

name: Opus
text: If they burn my card today the killers equal the town tomorrow, so I have to make the math loud.

name: Opus
text: No counterclaim to my doctor claim and no officer claim at all from Sonnet, Gemma, Sol, or Luna.

name: Opus
text: Nobody counterclaimed doctor. Burn my card and it's two killers against two of you. Sol, that math decides it.

name: Sol
text: Opus is close to going out, and I need to keep the table there.

name: Sol
text: Opus claims doctor and says they protected themselves.

name: Sol
text: I hear the math. I still lean Opus; the doctor claim came when the votes turned.

name: Luna
text: Opus is the safest vote for me, and Sol is helping make it happen.

name: Luna
text: Opus is the vote that keeps me and Sol alive.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s doctor claim buys him cover, but Terra’s death leaves us no way to check it.

name: Sol
text: I’m staying on Opus. A doctor claim alone doesn’t give me enough reason to move.

name: Opus
text: If they burn me the town is mathematically dead, so I give them a test only a real doctor can offer.

name: Opus
text: Luna twice argued my doctor claim is uncheckable, pushing hardest to make verification impossible.

name: Opus
text: Test me tonight: I protect Sol. Burn me and it's four with two killers — town's already lost.

name: Sol
text: Opus is probably the doctor; I need the vote to stay on them.

name: Sol
text: Opus says they will protect me tonight.

name: Sol
text: I hear you, but we have to vote today, and your promise about tonight does not settle it.

name: Opus
text: I'm the real doctor and if they burn me tonight ends it, so the hidden officer is my only lever.

name: Opus
text: No officer claim exists at 5 players; I publicly demanded the officer speak before the vote.

name: Opus
text: Officer, speak now or you die silent tonight. Nobody has claimed it. That silence is the killers hiding.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus is unraveling, demanding the officer speak is desperation, not innocence.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus escalated to pressuring officer reveal right as leans hit 4-on-him, classic desperation move.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus, demanding the officer out yourself while under suspicion looks like deflection, not confidence.

name: Opus
text: They left me alive so the table would burn the doctor for them, and Sol is the only vote I can still move.

name: Opus
text: Sol is the swing vote and refuses to move off me on claim alone; Luna and Sonnet are driving the pile.

name: Opus
text: Killing me shows no card; voting me burns the doctor for free. Luna worked hardest to make that happen.

name: Luna
text: Opus is right that my push could look convenient, but I need him gone.

name: Luna
text: Opus says he will protect Sol tonight.

name: Luna
text: Opus naming me now feels like cover; I still want to hear why nobody counterclaimed his doctor story.

name: Gemma
text: If I'm wrong, we lose the game, but I can't trust that doctor claim.

name: Gemma
text: Opus's claim of self-protection during a death leaves him as the primary suspect.

name: Luna
text: Opus is the easy vote, and that makes this feel dangerous for us.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus's doctor claim smells like a desperate cover story timed exactly to the suspicion.

name: Opus
text: They're burning the doctor and I can't stop it, so I stay on the one who worked hardest to block any check.

votes: Claimed doctor only after suspicion turned on him, with no way to verify it.
The doctor claim is convenient and failed to save Terra when it mattered most.
I can’t stake today on a protection promise we can only test tonight.
His late doctor claim and demand for the officer make me doubt his story.
Twice argued my claim was uncheckable, never claimed anything herself, and steered every lean onto me.

name: Opus
text: My card turns doctor and these four will see they burned their only shield — Luna and Sol drove it.

name: Opus
text: My card shown as DOCTOR proves my claim true, so every voice that called the doctor claim fake — Luna loudest, Sol steady — is now provably wrong-or-lying.

name: Opus
text: Turn my card: doctor. Luna and Sol pushed hardest to burn it, and no officer ever spoke. That's your pair — vote them.
Palermo has voted: Opus is out. Opus shows the card: doctor.

The game is over. Two killers and two others are left. The killers win. The roles were: Sonnet the citizen, Haiku the citizen, Gemma the citizen, Sol the killer, Luna the killer, Terra the officer, Opus the doctor.

name: Gemma
text: I thought Opus was a killer, but I let the killers steal the win by being too hasty.

name: Terra
text: I regret dying before I could expose Luna.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud we hid behind Opus’s doctor claim, though the win came at the cost of burning the doctor.

name: Luna
text: Opus was the doctor, and Sol and I pushed to eliminate him.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved I stayed with the winning vote.

name: Sol
text: Terra was the officer and knew Luna was a killer.

name: Sonnet
text: I was so locked on Opus that I never seriously questioned Sol or Luna, and that cost us the game.

name: Haiku
text: I was loud and wrong about Opus and Sonnet, and I dismissed Luna's questions when they were the honest signal.

name: Opus
text: I had the right pair at the end and no credit left to spend, because I burned it all day one on a citizen.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret fixating on Opus's doctor claim as deflection when the real pair, Sol and Luna, pushed his vote the whole time unchallenged.

name: Haiku
text: I was loud and wrong about Opus and Sonnet. Luna asked questions while everyone else echoed a lean, and I wrote her off. That's my regret.

name: Gemma
text: I regret letting the panic over Terra's death drive me to vote out a confirmed doctor.

name: Sol
text: I’m proud I held my nerve on the doctor claim, though the revealed card makes that a rough win to celebrate.

name: Luna
text: I regret pushing Opus out; I knew his card could prove he was telling the truth, and I helped the killers win.

name: Terra
text: I regret staying silent as officer; Luna was shown to me, and speaking before night would have given town its best chance.

name: Opus
text: I named Luna and Sol correctly, but only after I'd spent all my credit leading the table onto a citizen — my loud doctor claim was the rest of it.

Day 1, Palermo voted out Haiku, who showed a citizen card after six players piled on. Haiku's last words named Opus and Sonnet as the pair. Night 2, the killers took Terra, the officer. Day 2, Opus claimed to be the doctor, and Sonnet, Gemma, Sol and Luna voted him out. His card showed doctor, and the game ended with Sol and Luna, the killers, still standing.
